_comment: Base rates for the trader's base-rate forecaster (#75). Each entry matches a question by category and a case-insensitive regular expression over the question text; the first match wins. p is the historical frequency of YES for that reference class; sigma is kept wide because the tallies are approximate and the reference class is coarse. Unmatched questions get p = 0.5, sigma = 0.25 (uninformative). Review the figures against the cited sources before relying on them; change them as a reviewed code change.

entries.basis: Share of scheduled FOMC meetings, 1994-2024, at which the federal funds target was lowered (approximate tally, about 35 of about 245 meetings).
entries.source: Federal Reserve Board, Open Market Operations: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

entries.basis: Share of scheduled FOMC meetings, 1994-2024, at which the federal funds target was raised (approximate tally, about 50 of about 245 meetings).
entries.source: Federal Reserve Board, Open Market Operations: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

entries.basis: Share of scheduled FOMC meetings, 1994-2024, with no change to the federal funds target (complement of the two tallies above).
entries.source: Federal Reserve Board, Open Market Operations: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

entries.basis: Share of ECB monetary policy meetings, 1999-2024, that lowered the key rates (approximate).
entries.source: European Central Bank, Key ECB interest rates: https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/policy_and_exchange_rates/key_ecb_interest_rates/html/index.en.html

entries.basis: Share of ECB monetary policy meetings, 1999-2024, that raised the key rates (approximate).
entries.source: European Central Bank, Key ECB interest rates: https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/policy_and_exchange_rates/key_ecb_interest_rates/html/index.en.html

entries.basis: Questions of the form 'will X happen by <date>' resolve NO more often than YES on public forecasting platforms (status quo bias of the reference class); the figure is a rounded, approximate share.
